audit.why: The difficulty read is sound — Rumble owns levels 2-3, the lane goes even through 4-6, and Trundle takes over at two items. That matches the 48.66% win rate and the level chart without contradiction.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late spike quantifies Subjugate two different ways in the same matchup: spikes[3] and whys[6] say it 'steals a third of your armor and MR', while the late paragraph says 'a flat 40% of your armor and magic resistance for 8 seconds'. Neither number is in Riot's text, and they contradict each other.
audit.why: This is the spike the whole late game is built around. A player who trusts '40% for 8 seconds' plans a different fight from one who trusts 'a third', and both are guesses.
audit.corrected: Describe the mechanic Riot actually states: Subjugate steals health, armour and magic resist on cast, and the amount stolen doubles over the next 4 seconds. Cooldown 120/100/80 — the rank-1 window is two full minutes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three concrete interactions are absent. Pillar of Ice (E) is named as a threat but never given its cooldown (21s at rank 1) nor its real property — it is impassable terrain, and Rumble has no dash to cross it. Frozen Domain (W) is described only as a move-speed zone; Riot's text also grants increased healing from all sources inside it, which is the actual reason anti-heal is core. Chomp (Q) is an auto-attack reset, and the file describes it as 'resets on his auto', which reverses the mechanic.
audit.why: Point 4 is the key point. The healing amplification inside Frozen Domain is the specific hook that makes the Oblivion Orb timing matter, and it is the one thing the matchup never says.
audit.corrected: Pillar of Ice is a 21s rank-1 wall you cannot dash through — hold Flash for the pillar, not the damage. Frozen Domain amplifies all his healing, so Grievous Wounds is worth most while he is standing in it. Chomp resets his auto, so the wind-up is the tell, not the cast.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (Pillar of Ice cd 21/19.5/18/16.5/15, terrain; Frozen Domain 'increased healing from all sources'; Chomp autoReset)

audit.why: Liandry's into Shadowflame with Oblivion Orb / Morellonomicon is the right build, and the late paragraph already explains why percent-HP burn beats his resistance stacking.

edits.before: Trundle's late game is among the most punishing in the top-lane roster: Subjugate steals a flat 40% of your armor and magic resistance for 8 seconds, which means your Scrap Shield absorbs far less and the follow-up Chomp bites hit harder through your now-reduced stats. Never 1v1 him in a sidelane at 2+ items unless you are significantly ahead — you will lose the sustained brawl. Your role late is to drop Equalizer across objective chokepoints and fight in your team's composition, not beside Trundle. Build Liandry's into Shadowflame for percent-HP burn damage that does not care about his armor stack, and keep Oblivion Orb or Morellonomicon to cut his regeneration — his W healing and passive regen are the engine that lets him win long fights.
edits.after: Trundle's late game is among the most punishing in the top-lane roster: Subjugate steals your health, armour and magic resist on cast and then doubles that theft over the next 4 seconds, so your Scrap Shield absorbs less every second the fight runs. Never 1v1 him in a sidelane at 2+ items unless you are far ahead — you lose the sustained brawl. Your role late is to drop Equalizer across objective chokepoints and fight in your team's shape, not beside Trundle. Build Liandry's into Shadowflame for percent-HP burn that ignores his armour stack, and keep Oblivion Orb or Morellonomicon — Frozen Domain increases his healing from every source, so cut it before he stands in it.

notes: Both packet suspectNames are false positives ('Use Equalizer' and "Frozen Domain's" are correct). The real defect the name-scanner cannot see is numeric: Subjugate is quantified as 'a third' in two places and 'a flat 40% ... for 8 seconds' in a third, within the same matchup. None of those figures appear in Riot's text, so I replaced all three with the mechanic Riot does state (theft doubles over 4 seconds) rather than picking a number. If the user has a trusted source for the actual percentages, those lines are the place to put them back.
